newsitem.title: CHINA: Economy of China's Guangdong to grow 10 percent.
newsitem.headline: Economy of China's Guangdong to grow 10 percent.

text.p: China's booming southern Guangdong province expects to post 10-11 percent growth in 1996, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
The province would produce gross domestic product of 600 billion yuan, it said, quoting a forecast by the provincial statistics bureau.
Retail price inflation would rise by less than 5.0 percent, and industrial output would rise by 16 percent, with light industry showing faster growth, the bureau said.
For the first time in the past four years the province saw an increase in acreage under grain this year, without output certain to increase, it added.
Retail sales volume of consumer goods in the province would reach 270 billion yuan, up 11 percent over last year in real terms, the bureau said.

It noted that the investment structure had improved, with more funds flowing into sectors such as agriculture and water control, while investment in fixed assets was expected to grow by just 7.0 percent.
Farmers' per capita income was expected to reach 3,200 yuan, a rise of 8.0 percent, while incomes of urban residents would reach 7,520 yuan this year, up 2.4 percent.
